SATHER EARLSHERMANPIERCE was born in Bridgeton,New Jersey on
November29,1942,toPauline Boardly andEarlS.Pierce.He was reared
by his grandmother,Mary E.Morris,who was aCod-tearing woman,who was
active inSt.John'sCnited Methodist Church in Fordville,NewJersey
)eep within him,Earl always knew he was destinedto preach the Cospel.The
Holy Spirit called tohim at an early age.When he was twelve,he was baptized
in Laurel Lake and subsequently became a local preacher in the Methodist
hurch. He went on to receive his B.A. degree from ClassboroState College
RowanUniversity todayin 1965.During that year, he became the Lay
Reader-in-Charge at the Annunciation EpiscopalChurch in Lawnside,New
ersey.He continuedhis studies at the Philadelphia Divinity School,wherehe
receivedthe degree of Master ofDivinity in T9/O.InOctober970,Father
Pierce was ordainedasPriest and became a Vicar of the Annunciation Episcopa
Church in Lawnside
Father Pierce was employedas the Affirmative Action Officer for the South
Jersey Transportation Authority for more than ten years.At his death,he held
the position as Manager Political Liaison.
A strong advocate of civil rights and social change in the African-American
community,Father Pierce was ledby hisheart to seek political orfice many
years ago.In Atlantic City,he served as Fourth WardCouncilman,and for one
year asPresident ofCityCouncil
Prior to arriving in Atlantic City,he led an active and diversitied life.Forever
he champion of the underdog,Father Pierce was a Minister tor the Spanish
Migrant Workers under the auspices of the Diocese of New Jersey from 1963
until 1973.During his residence in Lawnside, he was also a police officer tor
he borough;President of the Lawnside Board of Education; a member of Tri
Borough Ministerium;Camden-Woodbury Clericus;Camden Convocation
Diocese of New Jersey;Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity;Black Elected and Appointed
Officials:Black Churchmen and Military Chaplains Association of the United
